expl.summary: This formula uses no jet-mass observable and no observable equal to (m/ΣpT)²: every if-statement tests an angular spread (λ₁, λ₂, ΣzΔR, Σz(ΔR/0.8)^½, e₂, e₃), a subjet distance, an N-subjettiness or energy-correlation ratio, or the pT of individual particles. It reaches a validation accuracy of 0.651. Mass information still enters through these shapes: neuron 2 falls with jet mass (rank correlation -0.74) and neuron 13 falls with (m/ΣpT)² (rank correlation -0.758) although neither tests them. The t score is built from size: it subtracts the compactness neuron 13 (ΣzΔR < 0.15, -47%), on which tops sit far below every other class, and adds the overall-size neuron 10 (λ₁ above 0.016, +26%); it follows ΣzΔR, λ₁+λ₂ and λ₁ with rank correlations of about 0.92. The q score is mostly the narrow, centred-jet neuron 9 (+56%), minus overall size (neuron 10, -18%). The g score adds neuron 2 (small angularity, hard 8th particle, +38%), neuron 9 (+22%) and the broad-jet neuron 1 (+13%), and subtracts neuron 5 (pT concentrated in the hardest particles, -14%), on which quarks sit highest. The W and Z scores add the elongated, compact scales (neuron 11 for W, +24%; neuron 7 for both, +13% and +35%) and subtract the wide-in-both-directions neuron 3 (-14% and -21%) and the off-centre spread neuron 6 (-10% and -15%). W and Z are separated by λ₁+λ₂: the intermediate-λ₁+λ₂ neuron 14 raises the Z score (+6%) and lowers the W score (-10%), and neuron 15 (ΣzΔR above 0.086) lowers the W score (-8%) more than the Z score (-2%).

0.title: elongated two-prong jet of intermediate spread (λ₁ 0.0043-0.012)
0.measures: Pushed up for λ₁ < 0.012 (its strongest term), τ₁ < 0.052, max ΔR(3 subjets) > 0.14 and e₃ < 8e-05, and pushed down for ΣzΔR < 0.08, λ₁ < 0.0043, total pT below 760 GeV, τ₂ < 0.018, max ΔR(3 subjets) > 0.19 and |Σz(Δη,Δφ)| > 0.0064; it is largest for jets with λ₁ between 0.0043 and 0.012, three subjet axes 0.14-0.19 apart and a centred pT. It rises with 1−λ₂/λ₁ and falls with planar flow, M₂, N₂ and τ₂₁ (rank correlations 0.569, -0.569, -0.546, -0.54, -0.528). W (1.93) and Z (1.90) jets sit highest, tops (0.35), quarks (0.18) and gluons (0.16) low; it is zero for 85.1% of gluons, 86.7% of quarks and 78.5% of tops, but only for 23.1% of W and 20.6% of Z jets.
0.role: It raises the W score (+9%) and lowers the g score (-6%). It does not enter the q, Z or t scores; the Z score, although Z jets sit as high on it as W jets, relies on neuron 7 instead.

1.title: broad jet (ΣzΔR above 0.11) at high total pT
1.measures: Pushed down for ΣzΔR < 0.11 (its strongest term), for a soft 8th-hardest particle (z₇ < 0.064) and for jets narrow in both directions (λ₁ < 0.0084 and λ₂ < 0.0011), and pushed up for high total pT (ln ΣpT > 6.4), τ₁ < 0.1, z₇ < 0.064 together with e₃ < 0.0005, and λ₂ < 0.0013. It rises with Σz(ΔR/0.8)^½, ΣzΔR, λ₁, λ₁+λ₂ and jet mass (rank correlations 0.572, 0.571, 0.569, 0.562, 0.554), although no if-statement tests the mass. Tops (1.26) and Z jets (1.11) sit highest, gluons (0.70) and W (0.66) in the middle, quarks lowest (0.31, zero for 67% of them; zero for 19.5% of tops).
1.role: It raises the g score (+13%), where it separates gluons from the quarks that sit lowest on it, and raises the Z score a little (+4%). It does not enter the q, W or t scores.

2.title: small angularity (Σz(ΔR/0.8)^½ below 0.11) with a hard 8th particle, falling with jet mass
2.measures: Pushed down for high total pT (ln ΣpT > 6.1, its strongest term), for Σz(ΔR/0.8)^½ > 0.11, for a soft 8th-hardest particle (pT₇ < 42 GeV and pT₇ < 54 GeV) and for z₇ > 0.052, and pushed up for z₇ < 0.053, λ₁ < 0.012 and λ₁ < 0.0072 together with max ΔRᵢ < 0.25. Overall it falls with the largest subjet-pair mass and the jet mass (rank correlations -0.745 and -0.74) and rises with M₂ (0.676); the mass is not tested, it is followed through Σz(ΔR/0.8)^½, λ₁ and particle pT. Gluons (3.53) and quarks (2.56) sit highest, above W (1.70), Z (1.39) and tops (1.23); it is rarely zero (4.2% of gluons, 23.7% of tops).
2.role: It raises the g score, where it is the largest input (+38%). It does not enter the q, W, Z or t scores. Freezing it costs 3.5 accuracy points, the most of any neuron.

3.title: jet wide in both directions (λ₂ above 0.0036) with pT at 0.2 ≤ ΔR < 0.4
3.measures: Switched off for λ₂ < 0.0036, by far its strongest term (share -0.406); once λ₂ is larger, it is pushed up for Σz(ΔR/0.8)^½ > 0.29, two subjet axes more than 0.17 apart (ΔR(2 subjets) > 0.17, also with C₂ < 0.1) and max ΔR(3 subjets) > 0.2, and pushed down for Σz(ΔR/0.8)^½ > 0.33 and λ₁ > 0.012. It follows the pT share and number of particles at 0.2 ≤ ΔR < 0.4 (rank correlations 0.709 and 0.70), λ₁+λ₂ (0.543) and (m/ΣpT)² (0.532), which it does not test. Tops sit far highest (3.32), then gluons (0.80) and quarks (0.39); Z (0.11) and W jets (0.01) are almost never on it (zero for 98.9% of W and 82.4% of Z jets, but for only 23.6% of tops).
3.role: It lowers the W score (-14%) and the Z score (-21%). It raises the t score only slightly (+2%), even though tops sit highest on it; it does not enter the g or q scores.

4.title: two-prong substructure (small N₂ and τ₂₁) with λ₁ above 0.0084
4.measures: Pushed up for e₃ < 0.00019 (its strongest term) and, less, for N₂ < 0.22, high total pT (ln ΣpT > 6.3) and λ₁ < 0.0068 together with 1−λ₂/λ₁ > 0.73; pushed down for λ₁ < 0.0067 and λ₁ < 0.0084, 1−λ₂/λ₁ > 0.71 and λ₂ < 0.00064. It therefore needs a jet that is spread (λ₁ above 0.0084) yet has small three-point correlation. It falls with N₂, τ₂₁, D₂ (β = 2), M₂ and the smallest subjet-pair mass over jet mass (rank correlations -0.686, -0.679, -0.665, -0.654, -0.628). Z jets sit highest (2.27), then tops (1.67) and W (1.47), with gluons (0.46) and quarks (0.24) low (zero for 81.4% of gluons and 88.8% of quarks).
4.role: It lowers the q score (-8%) and raises the t score (+5%) and the Z score (+4%). It hardly enters the g score (-2%) and does not enter the W score.

5.title: pT concentrated in the few hardest particles, small angularity
5.measures: Pushed up for total pT of the 5 hardest particles below 580 GeV, Σz(ΔR/0.8)^½ < 0.21, e₂ < 0.038 with λ₂ < 0.00028, λ₁ < 0.0022 and e₂ < 0.038 with z₇ < 0.075, and pushed down for total pT below 740 GeV (its strongest term), ΔR₀ < 0.063 and |Σz(Δη,Δφ)| < 0.038. It falls with the pT share of the 8th-hardest particle (rank correlation -0.738) and rises with the summed pT of the 3 and 5 hardest particles (0.722, 0.715). Quarks sit far highest (4.37); gluons (1.42), W (1.35) and Z (1.33) are in the middle and tops lowest (0.55). It is zero for 11.3% of quarks and for 30-38% of the other classes.
5.role: It raises the q score (+6%) and lowers the g score (-14%) and the t score (-16%). It does not enter the W score and hardly enters the Z score (+1%).

6.title: off-centre pT with widely spread subjets and large angularity
6.measures: Pushed up for C₂ < 0.036, max ΔR(3 subjets) > 0.18 and Σz(ΔR/0.8)^½ > 0.26, and pushed down for max ΔR(3 subjets) > 0.032 (its strongest term), max ΔRᵢ < 0.18, ΣzΔR > 0.088, λ₂ < 0.001 and |Σz(Δη,Δφ)| < 0.021. 6.role: It lowers the W score (-10%) and the Z score (-15%) and raises the q score (+9%) and the g score (+5%). It does not enter the t score, even though tops sit highest on it.

7.measures: Pushed down for Σz(ΔR/0.8)^½ > 0.35 (its strongest term), ΣzΔR > 0.087, λ₁ < 0.0047 and λ₁ > 0.0073, and pushed up for ΣzΔR > 0.1, ΣzΔR > 0.045 with D₂ < 2.2, max ΔR(3 subjets) < 0.16 and τ₁ < 0.087; the term Σz(ΔR/0.8)^½ < 0.42 also pushes it down. 8.measures: Pushed up for λ₂ < 0.0002 (its strongest term), λ₁ < 0.0055 with little pT at 0.2 ≤ ΔR < 0.4 (z(0.2 ≤ ΔR < 0.4) < 0.058) and max ΔR(3 subjets) < 0.2, and pushed down for max ΔR(3 subjets) < 0.11, Σz(ΔR/0.8)^½ < 0.19 with z(0.2 ≤ ΔR < 0.4) < 0.053, τ₂ < 0.017 and |Σz(Δη,Δφ)| > 0.0074.
